key_insight: A growth-inspired graph-generation strategy can synthesize mechanical lattices and pair them with a GCNN surrogate for fast inverse design of target stiffness.
engineering_relevance: This enables rapid topology optimization of architected materials by reducing reliance on repeated finite element searches while still achieving close agreement with simulation.
method: Use a discrete dot-matrix node set and sequential cross-layer/intra-layer growth rules to generate lattice graphs.
Represent each lattice as a graph and train a 3-layer GCNN with dual global pooling to predict compressive stiffness.
Couple the surrogate with structural sampling for inverse design and extend the idea to curved, nonlinear beam geometries.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports finite element evaluation of a 3x3x3 nodal matrix dataset and an inverse-design case where 1000 MPa target stiffness was predicted at 1042.43 MPa and validated at 1027.49 MPa.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the diversity and coverage of the generated lattice database, so generalization outside the sampled topology space should be checked carefully.
paper_title: Growth-Inspired Graph Generation and Inverse Design of Mechanical Lattices via Dot Matrices Database Augmentation and GCNN
